title: FakeState::record_application_receipt mutates before conflict detection
description: The in-memory WorkflowStatePort fake in abacus-core/src/ports.rs pushes the decision id onto self.receipts BEFORE calling self.apply, so a same-operation conflicting receipt (different after-revision) returns ConflictingOperation while having already cleared that decision from the derived pending_applications set. Same validate-then-commit defect class as the activation/opening/deactivation fixes in the credential follow-up, but outside that scope. Fix: compute key and content, check idempotency and conflict first, then push the receipt and commit together. Add a regression asserting a conflicting receipt leaves the decision in pending_applications. Test file is the ports.rs test module; run cargo test -p abacus-core plus clippy -D warnings and fmt.
close_reason: Validated current receipt path is validate-then-commit; added regression proving a refused revision-mismatched receipt leaves the projection pending. Core tests and clippy pass.

title: abacus-core: provider-neutral ports
description: Define the persistence, work, and runtime port traits that abacus-cli consumes and that abacus-state, abacus-work, and abacus-runtime implement. No provider types, no SQLite or subprocess knowledge. These traits are the seam every adapter implements; changes here are C1 or above and require cross-review.
design: FINAL REVISION 6 PLAN from Codex consolidated C1/C3 verdict (S1-S6 passed; six integration defects block landing). F1 Signal payloads: DirectiveKind Amend{instruction}, Pause{reason}, Abort{reason}, Answer{report, answer}; ReportKind Progress{summary}, BlockedWithReason{reason}; SignalBody::Request gains recipient ActorId plus bounded ask - all via a shared BoundedText validated newtype (1..=500, no control chars), not generic mail; unresolved() gains recipient filtering for Requests; test payload round-trips, recipient-scoped unresolved, idempotent content conflicts. F2 one authority snapshot: replace signal.rs ScopeText everywhere with canonical scope::ScopeExpr (SubjectRef::Scope(ScopeExpr), SenderFence.scope: ScopeExpr, delete ScopeText and its 300-byte cap); SenderFence (DecisionActor + CapabilityId + ScopeExpr) becomes THE reusable authority snapshot; AssignDecision, RetryDecision, DecisionRecord carry authority: SenderFence instead of bare actor; AssignmentRecord.worker becomes full DecisionActor snapshot so fenced mutations are historically reconstructible; ProfileActivation gains class: AuthorityClass. F3 decision subjects into variants: Accept{handoff, attempt, reason}, Reject{handoff, attempt, reason}, Revoke{attempt, reason}, Reclaim{attempt, reason}, Cancel{reason}, TransferAuthority{to, reason}; DELETE DecisionRecord.attempt field; RESTRICT lifecycle Revoke to Active only (Submitted revocation refused - architecture 479-487 conformant; a Submitted attempt is decided by Accept/Reject only) with table update. F4 profile validation hardening: reject duplicate ProfileName, duplicate registry descriptor IDs, duplicate grants per profile (the bundle-len bypass), bundle membership by exact unique SET, descriptor-bundle class consistency (AssignmentLifecycle=Exclusive, AttemptLifecycle=Fenced), authority compatibility (Exclusive requires Orchestrator, Fenced requires Worker, Shared either); new error variants; concrete duplicate-grant regression. F5 validated artifacts: validate_profiles returns Result<ValidatedProfileSet, Vec<Error>>; route becomes a ValidatedProfileSet method requiring an Exclusive descriptor, scanning ALL matches with loud Ambiguous defense, never first-match; occupancy derived by the set (any exclusive grant = Singleton); ProfileActivation constructed only through ValidatedProfileSet (private occupancy, no caller assertion). F6 evidence/handoff binding facts (attach repair for 9NH.3/.4 omissions to this revision): HandoffRecord gains clean_tree: WorkspaceDigest proof; SubmissionRefusalReason::DirtyWorktree{paths} and EditScopeViolation{paths} carry enumerated detail; Evidence gains argv Vec<String> structured command, verification_paths set identity, artifacts Vec<(WorkPath, ContentHash)>, environment_fingerprint Option<ContentHash>; update evidence.rs red-green tests accordingly. Requested regressions verbatim: noncanonical/undeclared Signal scope rejection; payload/recipient round trips; per-recipient unresolved filtering; every illegal decision-subject combo unrepresentable; Submitted revocation refused; worker-exclusive and fenced-orchestrator rejection; duplicate grant/profile/descriptor rejection; first-match impossible; forged shared occupancy impossible; clean/evidence identity facts preserved. Then Codex does one focused diff plus independent gates, then land 9NH.5 and 9NH.6 together.
notes: Revision 8 (terminal round A-D) complete, gates clean at 66 core tests, clippy, fmt. A: evaluate_acceptance aggregates the always-present AcceptancePolicy over the full evidence bundle - exact command coverage, no duplicates, same-command red/green pairing per command (the false-red/true-green aggregate attack is the regression), Standard-form evaluator, strict workspace-digest equality with distinct WorkspaceMutated; the single pair helper is now the per-command primitive; VerificationSet also rejects duplicate commands with its constructor regression. B: authorize consumes the durable ProfileActivation and returns the exact AuthoritySnapshot with the REAL granted scope (caller widening impossible); GrantDrift refusal validates activation against the current set; ActionContext distinguishes CurrentAction from AttemptBinding with fenced-only-at-binding enforced via ContextMismatch; AuthoritySnapshot moved to assignment.rs as the shared home. C: WorkflowStatePort gains handoff(id), decision(operation), active_occupants(profile), and typed PendingApplication carrying the full DecisionRecord; activation registers one stable AuthorityClass per ActorId with ActorClassMismatch, structurally preserving worker-cannot-accept-own-handoff. D: CommitVerifierPort::worktree_view returns WorktreeView (head, workspace digest, canonical DirtSet) over an injected HostPath; DirtyWorktree and EditScopeViolation carry PathSet; EnvelopeSnapshot is constructor-bounded at 64KiB with EnvelopeTooLarge. Awaiting terminal PASS.
close_reason: Provider-neutral ports seam landed after eight adversarial C1 rounds with terminal Codex PASS

title: Phase 4: abacus-runtime

design: Decomposition draft (mint as children when ports pass C1 and the transport ADR settles): (1) abacus-runtime crate scaffold plus facade implementing core RuntimePort over an internal adapter trait, with the fake protocol peer and fixture contract suite. (2) Herdr v0.8.0 process adapter: high-level CLI/JSON invocation, pinned identity/schema/protocol-19 verification against the lock (fail closed, protocol_mismatch evidence exists), api snapshot parsing to normalized observations including the blocked detector states, detector-manifest fingerprint check with no-silent-drift refusal. (3) Generation-fenced handle binding: opaque token privately encoding named-session/pane/terminal-generation; stale detection; explicit reassociate - re-association is the NORMAL post-live-handoff path per HPG.3 evidence (both generations rotate, counters reset). (4) Prompt/doorbell delivery: text-then-delayed-Enter path via agent prompt (0.8.0 fix), bound observation cursor for busy-agent second prompts - a generic wait may observe the FIRST completion, so attribute only via cursor or report DeliveryReport::Ambiguous, never retry on ambiguity; doorbell as content-free structural variant; no send-keys prompt fallback ever (lock property). (5) Launch: LaunchSpec to agent-start with explicit cwd/env allowlist, envelope delivery verbatim, startup/delivery deadlines, twice-validated-PID process facts via pane-process-info for forced stop. (6) Live compatibility lane: one explicit manual/pin-change lane replaying the HPG.3 v0.7.5-to-v0.8.0 corpus; hermetic default. Deps: 2-6 need 1; 4-5 also need the HPG.7 transport decision only insofar as worker Scribe reachability shapes the envelope contents; epic deps on hpg.3/hpg.4/hpg.6 already stand.

title: Resolve Linux Codex-to-Scribe transport in ADR-0003
description: ADR-first C2 resolution for the HPG.5 provider gate. On Linux, Codex CLI v0.146.0 visibly selected the exact custom permission profile and could stat the allowlisted XDG socket, but both a fresh TUI client and a host-launched official sandbox-helper client failed direct AF_UNIX connect with EPERM and delivered no payload. The pinned release source says x-unix-socket proxying is macOS-only and Linux managed-proxy seccomp blocks new AF_UNIX/socketpair creation. Until this is resolved, a sandboxed Linux Codex worker cannot reach Scribe and therefore cannot hold an ABACUS role. Draft ADR-0003 before changing seams. Preserve Scribe per-request authentication/authorization and reachability-is-not-authority; forbid danger-full-access, broad loopback/network grants, workspace request files or polling, global config edits, keystroke fallback, and routing Scribe through Herdr beyond its constitutional cap. Evaluate at least an inherited pre-connected descriptor with a disposable probe, a narrowly command-scoped host facade that cannot execute project-supplied verification commands, an upstream Codex Linux-parity enhancement plus repin, and explicit v1 scope reduction. Acceptance: C2 cross-review passes; the selected least-privilege transport and threat model are precise; fresh Claude and Codex sessions pass payload and fail-loud missing-reachability probes; affected architecture/migration contracts are updated; HPG.5 can then close. Evidence: docs/compatibility/2026-08-04-scribe-socket.md and official rust-v0.146.0 network-proxy/Linux-sandbox contracts.
notes: STATUS CORRECTION: ADR-0003 is at revision 5 Proposed, NOT rev4-passed - substantive composer, credential-provisioning, activation-case, and runtime-sideband changes post-date that pass. Rev5 adds: three explicit activation cases (operator-channel creation, actor-authorized rotation of an already-registered same actor/class, first-worker registration as an AssignmentOpening effect) with full-content activation idempotency regressions; bounded >=128-bit hex launch material bound to attempt+credential with a swap-defense refusal before provider mutation; StartupDelivery::Submitted naming reflecting that Herdr AgentPrompt success is submission not application, covering Envelope and secret in one submission with NotDelivered retaining the handle; corrected durability claim (no ABACUS-owned durable plaintext, but provider-owned transcript persistence is an accepted operator-visible residual bounded by revocation); and the pre-acceptance runtime gate narrowed to a disposable fixed-function prototype to avoid a Phase 1 dependency cycle, with production full-chain tests as GYH.5/KBP obligations.

title: Phase 5: abacus-cli vertical slice and abacus init
description: Implement abacus init onboarding and the single CLI vertical slice doctor, ready, assign, spawn, signal, evidence, submit, accept or reject, close on a disposable repository per docs/migration.md Phase 5, including explicit recovery for worker death, Scribe restart, stale lease, dirty handoff, and provider mismatch. No push, PR, merge, CI, or global hook.
notes: SUPERSEDES the prior runtime-rpc note (R5.5 security correction): runtime-rpc MUST NOT accept a client-supplied LaunchSpec - that would be arbitrary host execution and would defeat HPG.4. Its public stdin schema is a NARROW use-case request: repo-id, authenticated requesting actor credential, AttemptId, bound transient worker credential/replay identity, operation id/deadline - no executable, argv, cwd, environment, Envelope, or client-asserted authority snapshot. Host-side order: authenticate and authorize runtime:launch through Scribe/core BEFORE any project discovery, load persisted Envelope/Attempt/worktree facts, resolve executable/args/env only from operator-owned allowlisted provider configuration (request content may select at most a validated provider/profile identifier), then construct the internal LaunchSpec and call RuntimePort. Prototype gate must prove hostile executable/argv/path/env fields unrepresentable or refused and an unauthorized actor unable to reach Herdr.
